scope: the left big toe, toe 2 and the 1–2 web (left is the man's own; every view shows his left foot)

merged.text: Under toe 2 a crisp ledge rings the toe and the distal part steps out like a sleeve cuff with flaps at its ends, smooth above and ridged below: a thimble glued on. Plantar creases are soft infolds that fade at the sides; the skin never steps.
also: Under toe 2 a crisp straight step rings the toe where the smooth middle segment meets the ridged pad, a thin flap sticking out past the lateral outline: a thimble glued on, where a real toe has a soft flexion crease.
Under toe 2 a crisp straight step rings the toe where the smooth middle segment meets the ridged distal pad, with a thin flap sticking out past the lateral outline: a thimble glued on.

Under toe 2 a crisp straight ledge rings the toe: the distal part steps out like a sleeve cuff, with small flaps poking past the silhouette at both ends, smooth skin above and ridged below. A seam that no toe has.
Under toe 2 a crisp, straight step with jagged corner tabs rings the middle phalanx, smooth above and ridged below: a thimble glued on, the most artificial thing in the plantar view.
Under toe 2 a crisp, straight step with jagged corner tabs rings the middle phalanx, smooth above and ridged below, like a thimble glued on.
fixes: A real toe has a soft, slightly curved flexion crease there, with the same skin and ridge pattern running on either side of it.
Make the skin one continuous surface: a plantar flexion crease is a soft infold about 0.5 mm deep that fades out on the sides, with the ridges carrying on across it.
Plantar PIP and DIP creases are soft folds in continuous skin; the surface and the friction ridges run unbroken into and across them.

merged.text: The hallux plate is one milky pink from root to edge, with no lunula, no pink bed under a clearer plate and no onychodermal band, so it reads as tinted plastic rather than keratin over a nail bed.
also: No lunula on the hallux and no zoning in the plate: one pink-grey tint from fold to free edge, no pale crescent at the root, no pink bed under a clear plate, no onychodermal band. §1.4 asks for a visible lunula.
No lunula on the hallux and no zoning in the plate: one pink-grey tint from fold to free edge, with no pale crescent at the root, no pink bed under a clear plate and no onychodermal band.
No lunula on the hallux: the plate is one translucent pink-beige from fold to onychodermal band.
No lunula on the hallux: the plate is one translucent pink-beige from the proximal fold to the onychodermal band, with no paler crescent at its root.
The hallux plate is one even milky pink from root to edge: no lunula at the fold, no pinker bed seen through a clearer plate, no onychodermal band, so it reads as tinted plastic.
fixes: A real hallux nail shows a pale lunula crescent (about 3.5 mm) at the root, a pink bed through the clear plate, and a paler band at the onychodermal line before the free edge.
Show a whitish crescent about 3.5 mm deep emerging from under the proximal fold, its distal edge soft.
Show a pale 3.5 mm lunula crescent under the proximal fold, the pink bed through a translucent plate, a narrow amber-grey onychodermal band, then the opaque free edge.

merged.text: The hallux nail, the focus of most views, is a press-on: a rounded-rectangle tile in an even gutter inside one uniform raised rim, its edges standing proud of the lateral folds and the plate nearly flat across. A real plate domes and slips under its folds.
also: The hallux nail is a press-on: a rounded-rectangle tile set in an even gutter inside one uniform raised rim, its side edges standing proud of the lateral folds and the plate nearly flat from side to side.

The nails read as press-ons: the hallux plate is a rounded-rectangle tile in an even gutter with a gasket rim all round, margins exposed, nearly flat across. Real lateral folds swallow the margins and the plate falls away into them.

The hallux nail is still a press-on: a rounded-rectangle tile set in an even gutter with a thin raised gasket rim all round, its lateral margins fully exposed, its surface nearly flat across instead of falling away into the folds.

The hallux nail, centre of most views, is a press-on: a flat rounded-rectangle tile in an even gutter with a raised gasket rim, toe 2's the same; a real plate is domed and its sides slide under soft, uneven lateral folds.

The hallux plate (and toe 2's) is a flat rounded-rectangle tile set in an even gutter with a raised gasket rim all round, a press-on; its sides stay level instead of curving down under the lateral folds.
fixes: A real plate is domed (11 mm transverse radius) so its sides fall away under the lateral folds, which overlap its edges; the proximal fold is a soft cuticle roll, wider than the lateral folds, not one even rim.

The lateral folds overlap and hide the plate margins, the proximal fold is a broad soft lip whose cuticle lies on the plate with no gutter, and the plate curves clearly down to both sides (11 mm radius; toe 2 6 mm).
Dome the plate to its 11 mm transverse radius (6 mm on toe 2) so the sides dive under soft, uneven lateral folds that overlap it; the proximal fold is a low roll of skin with a cuticle, not a gutter.

merged.text: The hallux's distal segment looks plugged on: in profile the plantar outline drops in a hard V-notch at the IP crease and the groove rings the medial side. A real hallux arches smoothly from base sulcus to pulp, its IP crease dying out on the sides.
also: In profile the hallux's plantar outline is cut by a hard V-notch at the IP crease, the pulp hanging lower than the phalanx behind it as if a second tube were plugged on; a real IP crease is a soft, shallow dip.
In profile the hallux's plantar outline is cut by a hard V-notch at the IP crease, the pulp hanging lower than the phalanx behind it, as if a second tube were plugged on.

In profile the hallux pulp looks plugged on: the plantar outline drops in a hard V-notch at the IP crease and the groove carries on up the medial side as a ring, so the distal segment reads as a separate tube.
In profile the hallux's plantar IP crease is a hard V-notch ringing the toe, the pulp stepping down like a second tube plugged on; the clay confirms it is geometry, where a real toe dips softly.
The hallux's plantar IP crease is a hard V-notch that rings up the medial side, so the distal segment steps down like a second tube plugged into the first; the clay shows it is geometry.
fixes: A real hallux shows a shallow, soft dip at the plantar IP crease in an otherwise continuous outline, the pulp bulging smoothly out of it.
Under a resting hallux the outline arches smoothly from the base sulcus to the pulp; the plantar IP crease is a deep soft fold that shallows and ends on the medial and lateral sides.
In profile the plantar outline flows from the proximal phalanx into the pulp with a shallow, soft dip at the IP crease; the pulp swells gradually, with no stepped collar.

merged.text: Every skin surface wears one dark-outlined Voronoi crackle, cells about 0.4–0.8 mm (twice §3.4's toe cells), equally crisp on knuckle, shaft and pulp and running into the folds: crazed porcelain at native size, not the faint, directional furrows of real skin.
also: Every skin surface carries one dark-outlined Voronoi crackle, cells about 0.4–0.8 mm, twice §3.4's 0.25–0.4 mm for toes, equally crisp on knuckle, shaft and pulp and running into the folds: crazed porcelain at native size.

All skin wears one dark-outlined Voronoi crackle, too coarse on toe 2 and the web and the same on dorsum, pulp and fold: crazed glaze at native size, where real skin shows a faint shaded furrow network.
All skin wears one Voronoi crackle: dark-outlined polygonal cells about 0.4-0.8 mm, equally sharp on dorsum, pulp, folds and web; at native size toe 2 reads as crazed glaze.

All the skin wears one dark-outlined Voronoi crackle, equally sharp everywhere and running into the folds: crazed porcelain at native size on toe 2 and the hallux, crocodile plates in the web zoom; real toe skin shows a faint, shallow net.

All the skin wears one dark-outlined Voronoi crackle of 0.3-0.8 mm cells, equally sharp and deep everywhere and running into the folds: crazed porcelain at native size, crocodile plates in the web zoom.
fixes: Real toe skin shows faint, shallow furrows in a directional rhomboid net that softens on the pulp and deepens only over the joints, with pores between them.
Toe skin shows a faint rhomboid furrow network 0.25-0.4 mm made by shading, not dark lines, oriented along tension lines, turning into ridges on the pads and fine stretch lines on the web.
Toe skin shows a faint, shallow net of fine lines 0.25-0.4 mm apart, mostly rhomboid along the tension lines, low in contrast, softer on the pulp and stretched or lost in folds.

merged.text: From below, the hallux and toe 2 pads are straight-sided rounded boxes and the hallux pulp starts under a raised rim at its IP crease; real pulps are oval domes, widest near the tip, swelling softly out of a curved crease.
also: From below, the hallux and toe 2 pads are rounded boxes with straight, parallel sides, and the hallux pulp starts under a raised rim at its IP crease.

From below the hallux and toe 2 pads are rounded boxes with straight sides, the hallux pad capped by a raised rim at its IP crease; real pulps are oval domes, widest distally, rolling into the sides of the toe.
From below the hallux pad is a rounded box with straight parallel sides, capped by a raised rim along its IP crease; toe 2's pad is the same box.
From below the hallux pad is a rounded box with straight sides, capped by a raised ridge at its IP crease, where a real pulp is an oval dome.
From below the hallux pad is a rounded box with straight parallel sides, capped by a raised ridge along its IP crease.
fixes: Real pulps are oval domes, widest near the tip, swelling softly out of a curved flexion crease with no rim.
A toe pulp is an oval dome, widest distally, that rolls into the toe's sides; the IP crease is a soft fold, not a lip.
A real pulp is an oval dome, widest a little behind its middle and tapering to the tip; its IP crease is a soft fold with no raised lip.

merged.text: The 1-2 web ends in a ruler-straight horizontal margin meeting toe 2's wall at a right angle, a shelf between the toes, where a real web is a soft U-shaped saddle dipping between the toe bases.
also: The 1–2 web is a flat shelf: a straight margin that drops in a lobe to meet toe 2's wall at a square corner, with a hard straight crease where it leaves the hallux; a real web is a soft U-shaped saddle sunk between the toe bases.
The 1–2 web is a flat shelf: a straight margin that drops in a lobe to meet toe 2's wall at a square corner, with a hard straight crease where it leaves the hallux.

The 1-2 web ends in a ruler-straight horizontal margin about 8 mm long that meets toe 2's medial wall at a right angle: a flat shelf between the toes. The same straight edge shows in pair_hr.hallux_eval.png and the front view.
The 1-2 web's margin is a straight horizontal edge, a flat shelf between the toes, rather than a soft U-shaped saddle sunk between their bases.
fixes: A real 1–2 web is a soft U-shaped saddle sunk between the toe bases, its margin curving continuously into both toes.
A real web is a soft U-shaped saddle: the dorsal skin rolls over a rounded free margin that dips between the toe bases and curves up into each toe's side with no corner.
The web's free margin dips in a soft U well back between the toes and rolls smoothly into each toe's wall, shadowed in its depth.

merged.text: The hallux IP and toe 2 PIP wrinkles are one stamp, three or four identical, evenly spaced glossy grooves that bump the profile like bellows; knuckle wrinkles are uneven, broken and fade at the sides.
also: The hallux IP and toe 2 PIP wrinkles are one stamp: three or four evenly spaced, parallel, glossy-lipped grooves that bump the profile like bellows; real knuckle skin has a loose, uneven cluster of fine, branching wrinkles.
The hallux IP and toe 2 PIP wrinkles are one stamp: three or four evenly spaced, parallel, glossy-lipped grooves that bump the profile like bellows (see the medial view).

Knuckle wrinkles are one stamp per joint: three or four identical concentric arcs, evenly spaced and glossy-lipped, saw-toothing the profile like bellows. Real knuckle skin has an irregular cluster of fine creases of unequal length.
The hallux IP and toe 2 PIP wrinkles are one stamp each: three or four identical, evenly spaced concentric arcs with glossy lips, proud enough to saw-tooth the dorsal profile in the medial view.
The hallux IP and toe 2 PIP wrinkles are one stamp: three or four identical, evenly spaced parallel grooves with glossy lips, proud enough to bump the dorsal profile in the medial view, like bellows.
fixes: Real knuckle skin has a loose, uneven cluster of fine wrinkles that branch, fade and vary in spacing, without proud lips.
Knuckle skin carries a loose, irregular cluster of fine creases of unequal length and depth, some branching or crossing, fading at the sides and barely touching the silhouette at rest.
Knuckle skin carries a loose, uneven cluster of fine wrinkles of varied length, depth and spacing, broken and branching, fading at the sides and never bumping the silhouette.

merged.text: The hallux grows straight out of the ball with no toe-base sulcus underneath, so it has no root; a real sole folds deeply where the toe pad meets the ball.
also: From below the hallux flows straight out of the ball with no sulcus at its base, its only crease at the IP; a real sole folds deeply where the toe pad meets the ball.
From below the hallux flows straight out of the ball with no sulcus at its base; its only crease is at the IP.
From below the hallux grows straight out of the ball with no toe-base sulcus; its only crease is at the IP, so the toe has no root.
The hallux flows straight out of the ball with no base sulcus; a real sole folds deeply where the toe pad meets the ball.
The hallux flows straight out of the ball with no crease at its base; its only plantar fold is at the IP.
fixes: A real sole folds deeply where the toe meets the ball, a curved sulcus that sets the toe pad off from the forefoot.
Fold the sole deeply where the hallux pad meets the ball under the first MTP: a curved crease 1-2 mm deep with the toe's pad bulging distal to it.
A sole folds deeply where the toe pad meets the ball: a curved digito-plantar sulcus across the hallux base, deeper than the IP crease.

merged.text: The plantar friction ridges are straight parallel stripes at one angle across the ball, both pads and the phalanges, running through the creases like corduroy; real pads carry whorls or loops that follow each pad and stop at the creases.
also: The plantar friction ridges are straight parallel stripes at one angle across the ball, both pads and the phalanges, running straight through the creases like corduroy.
Friction ridges are straight parallel diagonal stripes over the ball and both pads, ignoring the creases: corduroy. A hallux pulp carries a whorl or loop centred on the pad.
Friction ridges are straight parallel stripes at one diagonal angle across the ball and both pads, running through the creases like corduroy; the hallux pulp has no whorl or loop.

The friction ridges are straight parallel stripes at one angle across the ball and both pads, running through the creases like corduroy; toe pads carry whorls or loops and the ridges bend at the creases.

The friction ridges are straight parallel stripes at one angle across the ball and both pads, running straight through the creases like corduroy, and line the sole's medial edge like machined grooves in profile.
fixes: Real pads carry whorls or loops centred on each pad; the ridges change direction between ball, phalanges and pads and break at the creases.
Each toe pad carries a whorl or loop centred on its dome, the ridges curving round it and broken at the flexion creases; on the ball they sweep in broad curves.
Toe pads carry whorls or loops centred on the pulp; on the ball the ridges flow in curved fields that bend and break at the creases.

merged.text: A thin raised glossy line arcs across the first MTP dorsum and notches the medial profile; a podiatrist reads a healed incision, not a crease.
also: A thin, raised, glossy line arcs about 15 mm across the dorsum of the first MTP and nicks the dorsal profile in the medial view: a podiatrist would read a healed incision scar, not joint creases.
A thin, raised, glossy line arcs about 15 mm across the dorsum of the first MTP and nicks the dorsal profile in the medial view: it reads as a healed incision scar.
A single thin, raised, glossy line arcs about 15 mm across the first MTP dorsum and notches the profile in the medial view: it reads as a healed incision, not a skin crease.
A thin, raised, glossy arc across the first MTP dorsum reads as a healed incision, and in profile shows as two staple-like ticks on the outline.
A thin, raised, glossy line arcs about 15 mm across the first MTP dorsum and shows as two staple-like ticks on the profile in the medial view; it reads as a healed incision, not a crease.

Dorsal MTP skin shows at most a few faint, broken transverse creases of differing length, recessed rather than raised, with no gloss of their own.
Over the first MTP the skin carries at most a faint, soft transverse fold that flattens out toward the sides, with no raised or glossy ridge.

merged.text: The dorsum in frame is a smooth, oily mannequin surface: no EHL cord onto the hallux, no slip to toe 2, no veins, the extensor ridges fading out before the MTPs.
also: The forefoot dorsum in frame is smooth: one faint extensor ridge fades before the MTPs, no EHL cord runs onto the hallux, no slip reaches toe 2, no dorsal vein shows. The anchor feet carry tendon and vein relief right here.
The forefoot dorsum in frame is smooth: one faint extensor ridge fades before the MTPs, no EHL cord runs onto the hallux, no slip reaches toe 2 and no dorsal vein shows.
No EHL cord rises over the first MTP or runs onto the hallux, no extensor slip onto toe 2, no dorsal vein: a lean soldier's forefoot would show them as low relief.
No extensor hallucis longus cord rises over the first MTP or runs onto the hallux, no slip runs onto toe 2 and no dorsal vein shows: the forefoot dorsum is mannequin-smooth.
The forefoot dorsum is a smooth, oily mannequin surface: faint extensor ridges fade before the MTPs, no EHL tendon runs onto the hallux, no slip to toe 2, no dorsal veins.

The EHL stands as a cord from the instep onto the hallux's proximal phalanx, the slip to toe 2 is a low ridge, and a few dorsal veins sit 0.5-1 mm proud, catching the rim light.

merged.text: The hallux and toe 2 are bald; a 40-year-old man's big toe usually carries a few dark hairs on its proximal phalanx, as the anchor feet do.
also: No hair: no tuft of dark hairs on the hallux's proximal phalanx and none on toe 2; next to the anchor feet the bald toes read young.
No hair: no tuft of dark terminal hairs on the hallux's proximal phalanx and none on toe 2, so the toes read young and scrubbed.
The hallux and toe 2 are bald: no dark hairs on the hallux's proximal phalanx or on toe 2, which reads young and groomed beside the anchor feet.
No visible hair: no dark tuft on the hallux's proximal phalanx and none on toe 2; bald toes read young.
No visible hair: no dark tuft on the hallux's proximal phalanx and none on toe 2, only a few tiny pale flecks at most; bald, clean toes read young and mannequin-like.
fixes: 8–12 dark hairs 5–8 mm long on the hallux's proximal phalanx and 2–4 on toe 2, lying flat toward the tip, as several anchor feet show.
Give the hallux a tuft of 8-12 dark brown hairs 5-8 mm long lying flat distally, and toe 2 two to four shorter ones.
8-12 dark brown hairs, 5-8 mm long, lie flat distally on the hallux's proximal phalanx, and 2-4 shorter ones on toe 2's.

merged.text: Toe 2's DIP crease is one long even groove with a bright lip across nearly the whole toe, a knife cut rather than two or three short soft creases.

Toe 2's DIP crease is a single long, even, bright-lipped groove across the whole toe, a knife cut.
Toe 2's DIP crease is one long, even groove with a bright lip across nearly the whole width of the toe, like a knife cut.
Toe 2's DIP crease is one long, even, bright-lipped groove straight across the toe, a knife cut, where a real DIP shows two or three short, soft creases.
Toe 2's DIP crease is one long, even, bright-lipped groove straight across the toe, a knife cut.

A DIP dorsum shows two or three short, soft, uneven creases that fade out before the sides.

merged.text: From below, toe 2's free edge shows past its pulp as a clear glassy sliver with jagged corners, and the hallux's free-edge corners glint past its pulp.

From below, glassy specks of the hallux free edge's corners glint past the pulp, and toe 2's free edge shows as a clear glass crescent beyond its tip with small spikes along its side.

From below, the hallux free edge's corners peek past the pulp as glassy slivers at the tip's outline, and toe 2's free edge shows beyond its pulp as an irregular glass rim.

merged.text: Both nails read as clear acrylic: a glassy, even-width translucent lip on the hallux, a milk-white bead on toe 2, highlights combed into jagged streaks, no grime line. Real toenails are satin and semi-opaque, with a narrow, irregular yellow-white free edge.
also: Both nails read as clear acrylic: on the hallux a glassy, even-width translucent lip, on toe 2 a milk-white bead, the highlights combed into jagged streaks, and no grime line under either free edge.

The free edges read as acrylic: the hallux's a thick, clear, layered band of constant width with a white line under it and a glassy lip in profile, toe 2's an even milky bead. A trimmed toenail ends in a thin, opaque, slightly ragged ivory rim.

The hallux free edge is a thick, clear, layered band of constant width with a white line under it, like an acrylic overlay, and a glassy rounded lip in profile; toe 2's is an even milky bead (French manicure).

A trimmed toenail ends in a thin, opaque ivory rim, slightly irregular in width and line, with a faint grey grime line under it; not a clear, rounded bead.

A real plate gives one soft highlight broken only by a faint ripple from its fine longitudinal ridges; the plate surface itself is smooth and only moderately glossy.

also: Toe 2 is a smooth tube widening steadily to its tip: no PIP knuckle wider than the shaft, no waist over the middle phalanx, no separate pulp bulb.

Toe 2 is an even tube from the PIP to the pulp: little knuckle swelling, no waist over the middle phalanx and almost no pulp flare in plan, a sausage toe.

merged.text: In plan toe 2 is still close to a parallel-sided tube from DIP to tip: the PIP hump now reads, but the waist over the middle phalanx and the pulp flare are each only about 1-1.5 mm (toe2 view, 47.6 px/mm).
The hallux is about 31 mm wide (plantar view) but only about 20-21 mm deep at the IP (medial view, 17.9 px/mm), so in profile it reads flat and spatulate rather than a round pad.

Everything reads too clean and young for a boot-wearing 40-year-old: no cuticle on the plates, no dry or flaking skin at the folds, no yellowing or thickening of the hallux nail, no grime under the free edges.

At native size the pulps read smooth and waxy, with no fine creases, dryness or flaking at the nail folds, and nothing shows wear; the toes read as a new silicone foot rather than a boot-wearing man's.
Taken together the toes read young, scrubbed and new: no grime under the free edges, no thickening, ridging or yellowing in the hallux plate, nothing of a 40-year-old man who lives in boots.

The first-pass skin material (declared, not scored) gives the dorsum a wet, lacquered sheen; it puts a glossy lip on every crease and so makes the stamped wrinkles and the MTP line read even more as carved grooves.
